newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch ECT faces protest over terminal takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: Dutch ECT faces protest over terminal takeover bid.

text.p: Dutch stevedoring group ECT said on Wednesday it still hoped to take over container handling at Rotterdam's Bell Mertens Terminal, despite a lorry blockade of its own terminal by Bell employees.

A spokeswoman at Bell, a unit of the bankrupt Irish group Bell Lines, confirmed that nearly all of the firm's 153 employees had blocked the gates of one of ECT's two terminals because they felt ECT's takeover offer was not good enough.
Bell Mertens' Gerda van Dijk said ECT was offering insufficient guarantees to safeguard jobs and the company was pinning its hopes on a better offer from a third party.
An ECT spokesman said the company planned to sit down with the trade unions involved and try and work out any differences.
"We're trying to find a solution," Jos Dekkers told Reuters.
ECT (Europe Combined Terminals) is owned by Dutch transport groups Nedlloyd, Pakhoed, Internatio-Mueller and state-owned Dutch Railways.
Waterford-based Bell Lines went into liquidation on July 4 with debts of around 40 million Irish pounds.
"We want ECT to withdraw their offer, and our employees are making that point. We have nothing to lose," Van Dijk said.
The blockade had not affected cargo loading and unloading at ECT but had stopped lorries leaving and entering the terminal, used for intercontinental container traffic.
The Bell Mertens terminal started operations about a year ago and handles around 260,000 containers a year, mostly for short sea routes from Britain and Ireland to Rotterdam.
Bell Mertens' Van Dijk said a deadline to save the terminal had been extended until tomorrow and that there were other parties interested in rescuing it.
The Rotterdam Port Authority issued a statement on Wednesday supporting the takeover bid by ECT, which also involves the unlisted Rotterdam firms of Steinweg and Lehnkering Montan.
